title: Journalists protest at Delhi police station over alleged sexual harassment

tea.why: Journalists protested alleged sexual harassment by police personnel during an Oct 3 protest and the police's failure to register an FIR.
tea.want: Protesters demanded the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against the accused police officer and an impartial inquiry.
tea.changed: Oct 5: Delhi Police detained 17 protesters, including a journalist, and registered an FIR against them, but they were later granted bail.

summary: On October 4, 2026, journalists and activists began a protest outside the Parliament Street police station in Delhi, continuing through October 5. They demanded the registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against Assistant Commissioner of Police Vivek Bhagat, who was accused of sexually harassing a woman journalist during an October 3 protest at Jantar Mantar. Protesters also sought an inquiry into the allegations and examination of CCTV footage. On October 5, Delhi Police detained 17 protesters, including one of the complainants, citing prohibitory orders. Police registered an FIR against the detained protesters, alleging unlawful assembly and damage to property. Later that night, a Patiala House court granted conditional bail to all 17 individuals.
demands: Registration of a First Information Report (FIR) against the accused police officer
Probe into allegations of sexual harassment
Examination of CCTV footage of the alleged incident
response: Delhi Police stated that complaints of sexual harassment were received and transferred to the Crime Branch for inquiry. Police also said that prohibitory orders were in force, justifying the detentions, and later registered an FIR against 17 protesters. The accused ACP was promoted, but later requested to withdraw from the new charge…

injuries.text: two of the accused, Dharmender and Samarth, alleged that they were beaten inside the Parliament Street Police Station…

updates.text: Scores of journalists and activists began a protest outside Parliament Street police station demanding an FIR against an ACP accused of sexual harassment.
Protesters continued their sit-in, having spent a second consecutive night outside the police station.
Delhi Police detained 17 protesters, including a woman journalist, from outside the Parliament Street police station.
The Delhi government issued an order promoting ACP Vivek Bhagat, the officer accused of sexual harassment, to Additional DCP.
Delhi Police registered an FIR against 17 detained protesters, alleging unlawful assembly and other charges.
ACP Vivek Bhagat requested to not be given the current duty charge until an inquiry into the allegations was completed, and the order was modified.
Two detained protesters alleged custodial torture, and their medico-legal certificates recorded injuries.
A Patiala House court granted conditional bail to all 17 arrested protesters.
